content:
I have formalized some automata theory and proved some results about regular and ω-regular languages in Lean4:

https://github.com/ctchou/AutomataTheory

The capstone result is the closure of ω-regular languages under complementation, following essentially J.R. Büchi's proof as presented by W. Thomas in his survey article (see the README for references). Many other results are also proved. On the regular language front, some results in Mathlib.Computability are re-proved, because I want a uniform treatment in my project and the formulations of NFA and DFA in Mathlib are not very convenient for my purpose.

Your comments will be appreciated.
Discussion thread: #computer science > Automata theory in Lean4

I've added McNaughton's theorem to my automata theory formalization:
https://github.com/ctchou/AutomataTheory/blob/e304484c07cb2723db043b087cfbfd596e7b0f37/AutomataTheory/Languages/DetMullerLang.lean#L187
The proof follows Choueka's approach (see README for the reference) and adds quite a few results about deterministic automata. This is about as far as I want to go in formalizing automata theory, at least for now. I'll try to get some of the results into mathlib or cslib. The discussion thread is still:
#computer science > Automata theory in Lean4
